# Tectova Methodology

Tectova is a multi-source fashion intelligence product. This page is the technical reference for the definitions used across show, brand, talent, season, fashion week, and ranking pages.

**On this page:** [canonical show records](#canonical-show-records) · [formats and categories](#formats-and-categories) · [seasons and dates](#seasons-and-dates) · [talent counts](#talent-profile-runway-counts) · [collection design](#collection-design-attribution) · [the Big Four](#the-big-four) · [fashion-week editions](#fashion-week-editions) · [profile badges](#profile-badges) · [rankings](#rankings) · [source map](#source-map) · [coverage and corrections](#sources-coverage-and-corrections) · [citing Tectova](#citing-tectova)

<a id="canonical-show-records"></a>

## Canonical show records

Publishers often describe the same collection in separate schedules, reviews, galleries, credits, and backstage reports. Tectova groups source records that refer to the same house, collection season, year, and category into one canonical show. The same collection therefore counts once even when several sources cover it. Duplicate house, show, and talent identities are resolved to single reviewed records before public counts are produced.

When counting runway shows, we do not include presentation, campaign, or other non-runway events that might be a part of a fashion week or another such event.

<a id="formats-and-categories"></a>

## Formats and categories

**Format answers what happened.** Runway shows count toward runway totals. Presentations, appointments, digital releases, films, lookbooks, campaigns, editorials, backstage coverage, street style, and trade or collective events are stored when useful but do not count as house runway shows unless separately supported runway evidence exists. Backstage material can remain attached to the relevant collection without becoming a runway occurrence. A presentation remains a presentation even if a publisher files it under “fashion shows.”

**Category answers what collection was shown.** Tectova's public record for the Big Four cities (New York, London, Milan and Paris) includes ready-to-wear, haute couture, menswear, coed, resort, bridal, pre-fall, and pre-spring runway collections. Categories are not weighted, and presentations never become runway merely because their collection is ready-to-wear. Broader runway intake is retained internally while its public coverage and presentation are developed separately.

<a id="seasons-and-dates"></a>

## Seasons and dates

The displayed year is the collection year, not necessarily the calendar year of the event. A September 2011 show can be Spring/Summer 2012, while a February 2012 show can be Fall/Winter 2012. Resort, pre-fall, pre-spring, bridal, couture, and other collection calendars retain their reviewed season labels. Exact event dates are kept separately, with precision recorded when a source proves only a month or year. We do not manufacture a precise day from a season label.

<a id="talent-profile-runway-counts"></a>

## Talent profile runway counts

Talent profiles publish one unweighted activity count: distinct, countable canonical runway records in Tectova's **Big Four Runway Record**, from 2002 onward. The retained computation also records broader evidence internally, but it is not a public comparative total while other cities lack equivalent schedule and cast coverage.

Non-runway source records are retained for identity, provenance, and future research, and sufficiently sourced records may support a public profile route. They do not increase public runway counts or determine runway relationships, rankings, badges, or runway scores.

For a model, “runway shows” counts one model appearance per canonical show. Evidence can come from a public cast or a linked public runway-model credit. When a cast explicitly assigns that person a different role, a model credit does not override the conflict. Opener, closer, and exclusive markers are booking details on the same appearance, not extra appearances. A model with two recorded nationalities is counted on both country pages, and country totals therefore add up to more than the number of models.

For designers and creative directors whose primary public record is collection design, the count includes active, reviewed design attributions attached to qualifying canonical runway collections. For other photographers, casting directors, stylists, hair stylists, makeup artists, and creative personnel, “credited runway shows” counts distinct canonical shows carrying that person's matching public cast or linked runway-work credit. A model credit on a creative profile is not recast as creative involvement, and an additive design attribution on a model, stylist, celebrity, or photographer profile does not become a walk or unrelated primary-role credit. Variant role spellings are normalized, merged talent IDs resolve to one survivor, and the same person-show pairing counts once when cast, work-credit, and reviewed design evidence overlap.

A profile's “seasons” count, like the Seasoned badge, includes every season label in its Big Four record, Resort and Pre-Fall included, while Unbroken Thread and The Sweep use Spring/Summer and Fall/Winter cycles only.

<a id="collection-design-attribution"></a>

## Collection design attribution

A show heading identifies the presenting house. It does not by itself identify the person, people, or studio responsible for designing that exact collection. Tectova publishes a `Collection design` block only when a reviewed, source-bound attribution identifies that responsibility for the specific collection.

The block distinguishes a person attribution from a studio attribution. A named person links to that person's Tectova profile. A named house studio links to the presenting house's brand page. An eponymous house and an identically named designer remain separate records, so both names can correctly appear on the same show page with different link targets.

Collection-design labels are not inferred from a house's current leadership, a generic role title, or a name search. An ambiguous creative-direction credit is omitted unless reviewed evidence establishes that it describes design of the collection itself. If no collection-design attribution is reviewed, the block is absent. Its absence does not mean that the collection had no designer.

Production contributions such as casting, styling, hair, makeup and photography are retained as source evidence, but they do not appear in the `Collection design` block. Tectova will publish a separate production surface only after those roles have a dedicated, reviewed, source-bound attribution path. This prevents a production or image-direction credit from being presented as responsibility for collection design.

Some designers receive a public Tectova profile because they have at least one reviewed collection-design attribution. Their `Documented collection design` section is a record of the qualifying Big Four runway collections currently attributed to them in Tectova's public record. It is not a complete career history. For a primary designer or creative-director profile, those exact reviewed person/show pairs contribute to the role-aware runway total and Collection Network; they never become model appearances. Resort and Pre-Fall qualify when the canonical is explicitly runway, passes the same date and Big Four city policy, and has a supported category. Official fashion-week calendar membership is a separate fact and is not implied by this count.

<a id="the-big-four"></a>

## The Big Four

The Big Four is a **city scope**, not a category label: it includes documented runway records from 2002 onward whose canonical primary city, or a separately approved reviewed appearance-city authority, resolves to New York, London, Milan, or Paris. An event-city fallback, a brand's headquarters, or participation in a travelling collection does not qualify a show by itself. Unknown cities and every other market are excluded from public counts and awards.

This is the beginning of Tectova's documented public record, not a claim that runway history began in 2002 or that coverage is complete. Coverage before 2012 is substantially thinner and less geographically even. A public total is a coverage-bounded record, not a lifetime or prestige score.

Profile totals and Show Club totals include every countable runway category within those four cities: ready-to-wear (RTW), haute couture, menswear, coed, resort, bridal, pre-fall and pre-spring. Categories are not weighted. Comparative model badges and rankings may instead use a separately declared, narrower women’s RTW Spring/Summer and Fall/Winter scope. In either case, presentations and other non-runway formats do not count.

<a id="profile-badges"></a>

## Profile badges

Tectova issues badges only from a dated, retained Big Four metrics run. The same role-aware canonical appearance facts feed profile counts, Most-Cast leaderboards and downloads, structured metadata, and badges. Model-only comparative editions (season Top 50, city Top 20, and period percentiles) use a selected reviewed women’s ready-to-wear **Spring/Summer and Fall/Winter** review frontier, not a complete schedule. Those comparative products remain gated and deferred until their exact frontier, cohort completeness rule, and coverage receipt pass together; resort, pre-fall, pre-spring and other non-comparative categories remain in profile and Show Club totals only. A missing or incomplete cohort issues no badge. Show Club uses the exact documented Big Four count printed on the profile for every supported talent role, across all countable runway categories. A Model ICON is a separately approved, stable-ID editorial roster. Show Opener is a positive factual signal only and is not a public badge: opener evidence is Models.com-concentrated and incomplete, so an absent opener marker is never read as zero or as evidence that somebody did not open a show. Each profile badge links here; absence of a badge is not a negative judgment.

Percentiles require at least three reviewed RTW appearances. The denominator and its population are retained with the run; the top 1%, 5%, and 10% cutoffs use ceiling rounding and retain ties at the cutoff. A person receives only their strongest percentile per period. Likewise, an aggregate season Top 50 suppresses city medals for that edition; otherwise only the strongest city Top 20 result survives. The Show Club ladder is 10, 25, 50, 100, 250, and 500 documented Big Four shows; its exact cohort distribution, facts hash and as-of date must be approved with an accepted coverage run before it is issued. The ICON charter records criteria, conflicts/recusal, freeze/version, correction/removal process and a review artifact; every recipient has a stable-ID, individual rationale. Each issued badge carries its run ID, computation date, ranking artifact and coverage-family context, so it can be traced to its retained input snapshot.

The public count is one person per distinct canonical show, using the model role for models and the matching craft role for creatives. It uses the same role normalization, duplicate resolution, publication holds, identity resolution, and suitability exclusions as every retained metrics consumer. It is a coverage-bounded record, not a prestige score, and applies no hidden city or category weight inside the Big Four.

<a id="fashion-week-editions"></a>

## Fashion-week editions

A city, season and year do not by themselves establish a fashion-week edition. A public fashion-week page exists only where Tectova has an explicit organizer or parent-edition identity and explicit memberships from that edition to published shows. The edition's city and season/year come from the parent record, not from a route slug or a sweep of shows in the same city and season.

An official schedule entry is not proof that a show occurred. Schedule entries can be displayed as schedule information; occurred/member shows are displayed only when an explicit, resolved membership connects them to the published show record.

<a id="rankings"></a>

## Rankings

**Most-Cast Models.** A model receives one count for each distinct canonical **women’s ready-to-wear** runway show in the reviewed Big Four season or year window. Only model roles and runway shows count. The headline metric is unweighted show volume. Ties are ordered by RTW opener count, RTW closer count, Big Four career count, and then name. City editions require a known reviewed city and remain coverage-limited unless that edition states its completeness gate.

<a id="publication-and-indexing"></a>

## Publication and indexing

Public pages read from hold-aware records. A reviewed publication hold can suppress a canonical show, source contribution, event, work, brand, or talent without deleting the underlying evidence. Merged identities publish only through their survivor. Records with unresolved source or identity conflicts fail closed rather than being promoted on inference alone.

Page availability and search-engine indexability are intentionally stricter than database retention. Thin but valid records may remain stored, while a brand or show route can be withheld until it has sufficient cast, image, source, or repeat-show evidence. Talent routes have minimum evidence thresholds, and the public talent directory is capped and sorted deterministically. These gates affect which pages are published or indexed; they do not convert weak evidence into a runway fact.

<a id="source-map"></a>

## Source map

Tectova's source graph contains records from well over ten named organizations and source systems. A well-documented show or profile can accumulate evidence from ten or more sources over time, but that is not a minimum requirement and it does not mean every field is supported by every source. Each source is used only for the claims it can establish, and source-level provenance is retained so a broad database-level source count cannot manufacture confidence in an individual fact.

| Source family | Examples in the Tectova record | What it can establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Official fashion-week organizers and calendars | FHCM, the British Fashion Council and London Fashion Week, Camera Nazionale della Moda Italiana, CFDA/FIT calendars, Copenhagen Fashion Week, Dubai Fashion Week, Berlin Fashion Week, FDCI, Seoul and Stockholm schedule publishers | Scheduled participation, city, event date, calendar status and sometimes format |
| Fashion houses and first-party production material | House collection pages, newsrooms, press releases, show notes, invitations, official videos and published credits | Collection identity, season, format, creative direction, venue, cast or production credits when explicitly named |
| Editorial runway and trade archives | Vogue Runway, FashionNetwork, NowFashion, WWD, Vogue Scandinavia and other established fashion, business and local publications | Independent event corroboration, reviews, dates, format, imagery and named participants |
| Cast and production-credit specialists | Models.com, Tagwalk and published production-credit pages | Named models and creative teams, role labels and sometimes opener, closer or exclusive status |
| Talent agencies | Verified agency roster pages, profile pages and public roster sitemaps | Profile identity, representation on record, measurements or biographical fields explicitly published by the agency |
| Personal and professional profiles | Official personal websites, public Instagram profiles, Model Mayhem, Fashion Model Directory and Model Society | Identity links and selected attributed profile facts; these do not independently prove a runway occurrence |
| Structured public knowledge and open data | Wikidata, Wikipedia and openly published schedule or archive datasets | Entity identity, aliases, geography, official links and corroborating structured facts, subject to identity review |
| Image and media provenance | House, editorial and agency galleries, Instagram posts and specialist archives such as Kendam | The origin and context of an image or media asset; an image source is not automatically cast or runway-format evidence |
| Manual primary-source and local research | House press rooms, local newspapers, specialist magazines, event organizers and agency casting announcements | Exact-show corroboration or named participants when broader databases are silent |

Models.com is important because it often provides structured cast and production credits that are otherwise difficult to find. It is not treated as universal or infallible: some pages are lookbooks, campaigns, presentations or mixed show packages; historical rosters can change; and a Models.com source is held rather than counted when its identity, category or physical-show destination is unresolved. The same field-level tests apply to every other provider.

Wikidata, Wikipedia and other open resources are enrichment and corroboration inputs, not shortcuts around primary evidence. A Wikidata identifier can help resolve a house identity, for example, but it cannot by itself prove that a collection was presented as a runway show or that a named person walked it. Agency and personal profiles likewise support identity or representation claims without automatically creating runway appearances.

<a id="sources-coverage-and-corrections"></a>

## Coverage, source decisions, and corrections

Tectova combines first-party schedules and house material with established editorial and specialist sources. A source is used for the field it can actually prove: an official schedule may establish date and format, a gallery may establish imagery, and a credit source may establish cast or creative roles. Inclusion on a calendar, archive, or generic “shows” page is not by itself proof of a runway format. Conflicts are reviewed at the event and source level rather than resolved by source count.

Missing nationality, gender, agency, city, category, date, cast, or image data is left missing instead of inferred. Agency relationships are described as “on record” unless dated evidence proves they are current. Current-season figures can rise as schedules finish and sources publish their credits. Historical coverage is strongest where source archives are complete, particularly across the Big Four, and should not be read as universal coverage of every market or career.

Corrections preserve provenance. Duplicate identities are merged, incorrect source contributions can be detached or held, and reversible change journals record reviewed data repairs. Public totals and ranks are regenerated from the corrected graph, so later editions may change without rewriting historical source evidence.

To report a factual correction or a gap in this record, email [support@tectova.com](mailto:support@tectova.com). Please include:

- the affected Tectova URL;
- what is incorrect, incomplete, or missing;
- your proposed correction; and
- a supporting source when available.

Reports are reviewed, and verified factual errors are corrected. We do not promise an individual response or a timetable for review.

<a id="citing-tectova"></a>

## Citing Tectova

When reporting figures or analysis from Tectova, credit Tectova and link to the page or methodology supporting the claim. Include the displayed update date where relevant.

Suggested citation: *Tectova, “[page title],” tectova.com/[path], accessed [date].*

When quoting a figure, retain the geography, category, and as-of date displayed on the supporting page. Counts describe documented source-backed records, not complete industry or career totals.
